profile.tagline: I design end-to-end data and AI systems: from data ingestion (ETL, SQL and NoSQL databases) to models, RAG chatbots and decision-making dashboards.
about: Engineering student in applied mathematics at CY Tech (apprenticeship, 2026–2029), I am an apprentice Data Scientist / Engineer at Safran Aircraft Engines.

After a Bachelor of Technology in Data Science at the University of Lille, I have worked across the full data value chain: engineering (ETL, data warehouses, NoSQL), modelling (statistical, machine learning, deep learning) and reporting (BI, data visualisation).
My internships at Inventiv IT (legal RAG chatbot) and then at Renault Group (supply chain chatbots) gave me hands-on experience with LLMs, semantic search and prompt engineering.

projects.title: Land Value Prediction
projects.subtitle: Decision-making tool, statistical modelling and AI on over 20 million rows
projects.context: Bachelor of Technology in Data Science · University of Lille
projects.summary: From data engineering to reporting: a pipeline over +20M transactions, three families of models compared and a decision-making dashboard.
description: An end-to-end project around real estate transactions: data engineering on over 20 million rows, then modelling to predict land values.
On the data engineering side, an ETL process feeds a data warehouse and a NoSQL layer. On the modelling side, three approaches are compared: statistical, machine learning and deep learning.
Results are presented in a dashboard (number of sales, price per m², total land value by municipality) and a SHAP analysis on 2,000 properties sheds light on the impact of each variable on price.
highlights: +20M rows processed
ETL pipeline, data warehouse and NoSQL
Statistical vs machine learning vs deep learning
Prediction interpretability with SHAP

projects.title: Credit Scoring & Deployment
projects.subtitle: Machine learning models explained with SHAP, in an interactive simulator
projects.context: Bachelor of Technology in Data Science · Data Mining
projects.summary: A complete data mining process, from training models to deploying a simulator that explains each of its decisions.
description: A complete data mining process: training machine learning models for credit scoring, then deploying them in an interactive simulator.

The simulator takes six key variables (remaining debt, interest rate, credit mix, annual income, average delay, credit utilisation rate) and displays the decision alongside a SHAP chart showing the weight of each variable.
highlights: Training machine learning models for credit scoring
Deployed in an interactive Gradio interface
Explainable decisions: variable impact via SHAP

projects.title: Legal RAG Chatbot for Lawyers
projects.subtitle: Semantic search over French law
projects.summary: A RAG assistant that retrieves relevant passages from French law via semantic search before having an LLM generate the answer.
description: Design of a RAG (Retrieval-Augmented Generation) chatbot for lawyers: the question is vectorised, the closest passages of law are retrieved from an index, then provided as context to an LLM.
An embedding model benchmark was conducted, with CamemBERT achieving +60% accuracy. The system is exposed via a Gradio interface.
highlights: Encoding of +800K lines of French law
Embeddings benchmark: CamemBERT, +60% accuracy
FAISS vector index for semantic search
Prompt engineering (Gemini) and Gradio interface

images.alt: Pipeline diagram: French law is encoded with CamemBERT and indexed in FAISS; a question is searched in the index then sent to Gemini, and the answer appears in Gradio.
images.caption: Simplified pipeline: indexing French law, then querying

projects.title: SQL to NoSQL Migration
projects.subtitle: From SQLite to MongoDB and Neo4j
projects.context: Bachelor of Technology in Data Science · Databases
projects.summary: Migration of a relational database to a document model (MongoDB) and a graph model (Neo4j).
description: Migration of a relational SQLite database to two NoSQL models: MongoDB for documents and Neo4j for graphs.
The graph model makes relationships between entities directly queryable, whereas a relational database relies on joins.
highlights: Moving from a relational schema to a document model
Graph modelling with Neo4j

projects.title: This Portfolio: from PHP/MySQL to React/FastAPI
projects.subtitle: Two versions, one shared content base
projects.context: Final-year project (BUT S6), then personal rebuild
projects.summary: v1 (PHP/MySQL, defended on 10/02/2026) was rebuilt as a decoupled architecture: a tested FastAPI back-end and a React/TypeScript front end.
description: Version 1 (defended on 10/02/2026): PHP/MySQL site with MCD/MLD modelling, CRUD back-office, filters and project pages, built over four months with generative AI tools (Claude Code, Gemini).

Version 2, what you're viewing now: a REST FastAPI API (SQLAlchemy, JWT, pytest tests) and a React/TypeScript front end, containerised with Docker and verified by GitHub Actions CI. If the API is unavailable, the front end falls back to a static export of the same content.
highlights: Typed REST API: FastAPI and Pydantic v2
JWT auth, rate limiting, anti-spam honeypot field
Automated pytest tests and GitHub Actions CI
Responsive, accessible front end with light and dark themes
